feed.subtitle: Research papers and global crypto regulation, at a glance
feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: FINCOSMOS: An open-world evaluation framework for finance agents
entry.summary: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper introduces FINCOSMOS, an open-world framework for evaluating language agents on financial tasks. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy generated from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked, while the agent must gather data from the Web and build its own backtest under a data cutoff. Grading uses programs that verify point-in-time correctness and recompute metrics, along with 15 veto checks. In 150 sessions, no session was accepted, and human experts attributed 88.33% of failures to the agents.

entry.title: Credibility Clustering for Experience Rating: Automating Risk Group Allocation in Group Life Insurance
entry.summary: Credibility Clustering for Experience Rating: An Automated Approach to Risk Group Allocation in Group Life Insurance arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper proposes a data-driven method called credibility clustering, which combines the multidimensional Bühlmann-Straub model with k-means clustering to automate the allocation of insured groups into risk groups in group life insurance. Credibility weights account for the varying statistical significance of experience data. Using real-world data from a major European insurer, the authors report that the framework outperforms two k-means benchmark variants in viability, temporal stability, and handling of statistical reliability.

entry.title: A bounded LLM research loop for quant finance, reporting two dozen campaigns, most failing.
entry.summary: Hard to Fool: A Bounded LLM Research Loop for Quantitative Finance, and What Two Dozen Campaigns Found arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper presents Autonomous Quant Researcher, an open-source loop in which a language model proposes strategy changes as fixed-vocabulary declarative JSON while trusted code decides acceptance. Evaluation uses immutable chronological data with a single-use holdout, multiple conjunctive gates, duplicate refusal, and a hash-chained ledger of all results. The authors report every campaign to date; most hypotheses fail, and one language-model survivor that passed discovery and validation fell from Sharpe ratios near 3 to 0.26 on its holdout.

entry.title: Constrained Defined-Contribution Pension Management: A Neural Network Method with Trading Limits
entry.summary: Constrained defined-contribution pension management: A reparameterized neural network approach arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper studies how a defined contribution pension member should invest when trading is restricted, using a two-factor financial market model. The participant can invest in cash, two nominal bonds, an inflation-linked bond and a stock index, and can buy term life insurance against pre-retirement death. The authors allow a general closed, convex trading constraint set, covering cases such as no short-selling and no borrowing. They propose a reparameterized neural network method based on Lagrangian duality to compute bounds on the value function, and calibrate it with U.S. data. The method yields a smaller duality gap than benchmark methods, and the constraints substantially change wealth accumulation, portfolio strategies and insurance demand compared with the unconstrained solution.

entry.title: A general method for explicit quantile representations
entry.summary: A general technique for explicit quantile representations arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proves that exact quantile integrals of strictly positive real-analytic densities admit contours that do not depend on the probability level. It gives explicit constructions covering five broad distribution families. Using forward functions, it also derives a finite-interval representation of Black-Scholes implied volatility.

entry.title: Chain-ladder reserving with exponential seniority weighting
entry.summary: Exponential Seniority Weighting Chain-Ladder Reserving arXiv · Nov 4, 2026The paper proposes a tractable state-space version of the chain-ladder model in which the dynamics act along the accident year axis, making accident years dependent. This formulation introduces exponential seniority weighting when estimating chain-ladder factors and provides an analytical likelihood representation. It allows computation of seniority-weighted chain-ladder reserves and their prediction uncertainty, with the one-year uncertainty available in closed form and total uncertainty obtained via Monte Carlo simulation from the likelihood.

entry.title: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? How Working Conditions Relate to AI Exposure
entry.summary: Dull, Dirty, Dangerous? Working Conditions and the Limits of Occupational AI Exposure arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper uses 21 O*NET items across 754 US occupations to examine how dull, dirty, and dangerous working conditions relate to occupational AI exposure. Higher exposure is associated with lower condition scores under both an LLM-based measure and AIOE. After adjusting for physical demands, education, training and experience, and wages, the composite association shrinks, with the LLM-based confidence interval including zero.

entry.title: Does Frontier AI Make Cyber Defense Stronger? Evidence from Project Glasswing
entry.summary: Does Frontier AI Strengthen Cyber Defense? Evidence from Project Glasswing arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper studies the effects of giving a small group of large US tech firms early access to Claude Mythos Preview, an AI model for finding software vulnerabilities, under Project Glasswing. Firms with access more than doubled their publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and disclosed about 150 percent more high-impact flaws, while fix speed stayed the same. The share of vulnerabilities exploited within a month of disclosure fell by about two thirds, while the number exploited did not change.

entry.title: Decision Models: Scalable AI Stand-ins for Human Economic Behaviour
entry.summary: Decision Models as Scalable Economic Surrogates that Capture Human Variation arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper evaluates Decision Models (DMs), a new class of AI models that quickly return probability distributions over fixed options, as substitutes for humans in economic simulations and surveys. The authors compare 10 DMs with 8 Large Language Models (LLMs) across a household spending survey, classic economic games, and a labour-market field experiment. The top-performing DMs reproduce the variation in human responses more closely than LLMs in all three settings, and they run roughly ten times faster than the fastest LLM and can be far cheaper.

entry.title: Wallet Identity as a Predictive Feature in Hyperliquid Order Flow
entry.summary: Beyond Anonymous Order Flow: Wallet Identity as a Feature for Short-Horizon Return Prediction arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper uses Hyperliquid's Level-4 data to reconstruct full-depth order books from consensus-ordered messages and tests whether pseudonymous wallet identity helps predict short-horizon returns. The July 1–27, 2026 dataset covers 17.1 billion messages, 14.3 million aggressive orders from 147,113 wallets, and $84.3 billion in taker notional across ten markets. In three model markets, wallets' notional-weighted ten-second markout rankings persist across adjacent ten-day windows, and on a 100-millisecond grid, eleven features describing previously top-scored wallets raise one-second out-of-sample R2 from 10.88%.

entry.title: Reducing Return Drag and Regime Switching in Sector Rotation: An Asymmetric Downside-Risk Nested Clustered Optimization Framework
entry.summary: Mitigating Return Drag and Regime Whipsaws in Sector Rotation: An Asymmetric Downside-Aware Nested Clustered Optimization Framework arXiv · Nov 4, 2026This paper addresses two weaknesses in sector rotation strategies: symmetric variance penalizes upside and downside equally, causing return drag, and Hidden Markov Model regimes switch too often, raising turnover. The authors propose Asym-Sticky-NCO, which combines a Bawa-Lindenberg downside semi-covariance matrix with a Gaussian HMM that has a persistence prior, applied to all 11 S&P 500 GICS sectors. In 65 out-of-sample months from August 2020 to December 2025, the framework reports a 13.41% CAGR and a 14.22% maximum drawdown, with regime switches cut from 16 to 4 and monthly turnover reduced from 60.78% to 30.48%.

entry.title: Fintech adoption and bank profitability and stability, with cost efficiency as a mediator in Bangladeshi banks
entry.summary: FinTech Adoption, Bank Profitability, and Stability: The Mediating Role of Operational Cost Efficiency in Bangladesh's Commercial Banking Sector arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This study uses a balanced panel of 30 Bangladeshi commercial banks from 2015 to 2024 to examine how a composite FinTech Adoption Index affects profitability (ROE) and stability (ln(Z-score)). It also tests whether operational cost efficiency (cost-to-income ratio) mediates these effects, using a two-step System GMM approach. Adoption shows no significant relationship with profitability, stability, or cost efficiency. Results from an entropy-weighted alternative measure vary with how FinTech is measured.

entry.title: Overall Calibration May Hide Undercoverage in Stress States: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals Under Recurring Financial Stress
entry.summary: Aggregate Calibration Can Mask Stress-State Undercoverage: Bounded-Memory Forecast Intervals under Recurrent Financial Stress arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines how judging sequential financial range forecast intervals only by aggregate coverage can mislead when calibration memory is bounded. The authors hold the model, score, update rule and memory budget fixed while varying which historical residuals are kept. A recent-only first-in, first-out buffer is near nominal overall but undercovers substantially in high-volatility states, whereas methods that retain state-specific history achieve lower interval scores during stress periods.

entry.title: Safe portfolio learning from untrusted predictions, with abstention and polarity failure
entry.summary: Safe Portfolio Learning from Untrusted Predictions: Signed Trust, Abstention, and Cross-Universe Polarity Failure arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies how to use machine predictions in portfolio decisions when their economic direction and reliability are uncertain and feedback is delayed. A controller chooses among Safe, Follow, and Reverse actions, learning signal orientation, while evidence gating, a delayed collateral budget, and a protected capital split limit risk. On a frozen 82-stock holdout, the pre-specified Reverse orientation did not outperform Equal Weight, and a post-holdout diagnostic showed that flipping the sign to Follow also gave no return edge. The contribution is safe adaptive use of untrusted predictions rather than demonstrated alpha.

entry.title: CosmosAlpha: Graph-Based Search for AI-Driven Stock Factor Discovery
entry.summary: CosmosAlpha: Multi-Relational Graph Search with Pareto-Guided Exploration for LLM-Driven Alpha Mining arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper presents CosmosAlpha, a framework that uses large language models to discover predictive alpha factors for quantitative finance. It organizes discovered factors into a multi-relational graph capturing generation lineage, expression-structure similarity, and cross-sectional exposure correlation, and propagates search utilities across this graph. On CSI 300 and CSI 500, the graph-based variant achieves the best mean rank across seven predictive and portfolio metrics and outperforms its MCTS-based counterpart on every reported metric.

entry.title: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market
entry.summary: Thinking Fast, Trading Late: System One Decision Models vs the Market arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper examines whether the stock-return predictability of large language models reading company news survives strict tests that rule out look-ahead, memorization and selection. The authors propose OLIVIA, a testing protocol, and apply it to non-generative language models that give probabilities for questions about S&P 500 news, including an open-weights model fine-tuned on 2024–2025 data and three commercial models. Results show the fine-tuned model's signal replicated on validation quarters but weakened on the blinded test period. The commercial models' readings match the overnight move to the open but not the move afterwards, indicating the news is priced before a trader can act on it. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose OLIVIA, a pre-registered protocol, and report that LLM news signals decay on a blinded test and are priced before the open.

entry.title: Multidimensional Analyst Views Behind Target-Price Changes: LLM-Based Outlook Representation
entry.summary: Multidimensional Views Behind Target-Price Revisions: An LLM-Based Representation of Analyst Outlooks arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper proposes an LLM-based method that extracts analysts' views from research reports as question-based outlook scores on dimensions such as earnings, valuation, and industry conditions, with supporting evidence. In walk-forward evaluation, these scores improve prediction of subsequent target-price revisions beyond current-revision momentum and sector differences. They also outperform financial dictionary and FinBERT sentiment measures.

entry.title: Can LLM Research Agents Reliably Judge Whether Models Are Predictable? Tests in Simulated Worlds With Planted Signals
entry.summary: Are LLM Research Agents Reliable Judges of Predictability? Evidence from Planted-Signal Worlds arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The authors test whether large language model research agents correctly decide if a forecasting model beats a static benchmark, using simulated worlds where a signal is planted. The agents detected weak signals more often than a pre-specified out-of-sample test, largely because they accepted weaker evidence. They also claimed predictability too often in worlds with no signal. The authors conclude the verdicts are informative but require a neutral brief, a decision rule set outside the agent, and a sealed holdout.

entry.title: PanelGP: a probabilistic model linking stock traits and economic conditions to returns and risk
entry.summary: PanelGP: A Probabilistic Factor Model for Asset-Return Panels arXiv · Nov 3, 2026PanelGP is a conditional factor model for large panels of stock returns, where firm characteristics set factor loadings and economic conditions set expected factors, both estimated with Gaussian-process priors. It nests instrumented principal component analysis (IPCA) and jointly forecasts expected returns and their covariance matrix. On S&P 500 constituents from 1995 to 2024, nonlinear loadings rank stocks better than affine loadings and yield higher Sharpe ratios than IPCA, though predicted variances are too compressed.

entry.title: Worst-case risk measures over overlapping Bregman–Wasserstein balls
entry.summary: Robust distortion riskmetrics over Bregman--Wasserstein balls and their intersections arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies worst-case values of distortion riskmetrics over Bregman–Wasserstein balls around a reference distribution. Unlike the squared 2-Wasserstein distance, these divergences can penalize upward and downward deviations differently. For strictly convex generators, it gives a one-dimensional dual representation and characterizes when the supremum is attained. The analysis is extended to intersections of such balls and illustrated numerically.

entry.title: Decomposing Model Rank Reversals Under Time-Varying Data: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability
entry.summary: Decomposing Rank Reversals under Temporal Nonstationarity: Alignment, Aggressiveness, and Instability arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper studies why model performance rankings reverse across different training windows when data is temporally nonstationary. The authors decompose out-of-sample R² into target alignment, miscalibrated aggressiveness, and predictive instability within a model-agnostic framework. They derive closed-form optimal memory equations for ridge regression under local drift and extend the guarantees to complex models via surrogate bounds. Benchmarking 14 linear, tree-based, and neural models on large financial panels, they find rank reversals are driven by predictable surges in miscalibrated aggressiveness.

entry.title: Honest Small Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Fixes
entry.summary: Honest Small Decision Models for Finance: Scale, Specialization Collapse, and Mixed-Corpus Remediation arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper trains small language models from 0.8B to 32B parameters to give fast, probability-based financial decisions in a single forward pass, using one fixed LoRA recipe. Narrow fine-tuning reduces general decision ability, while training on a mixed corpus keeps multiple competencies in one adapter. On real-outcome financial return questions, the models match a simple baseline in accuracy but produce well-calibrated, appropriately flat probabilities.

entry.title: Penalize the Common Trade: A Collision-Aware Layer for Learned Portfolios
entry.summary: Penalize the Common Trade: A Collision-Aware Layer for Learned Portfolios arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper argues that learning systems sharing data, objectives, or representations can make nearly identical trades, creating a "signal collision." A linear-impact game shows allocators take on too much common exposure, and an overlap-dependent toll can recover the social optimum. The authors propose a simple post-model layer that penalizes loading on the recent common return mode, which lowered maximum drawdown in a panel of ten liquid cross-asset ETFs, though the drawdown-improvement confidence interval includes zero.

entry.title: Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model: a statistical methods paper on variable selection and model specification
entry.summary: Specification LASSO and a Flexible Characteristics-Based Asset Pricing Model arXiv · Nov 3, 2026This paper studies a partially linear semiparametric additive model that allows interactions among variables in high-dimensional settings. The authors propose the Specification LASSO (S-LASSO), a two-step method combining LASSO and Adaptive Group LASSO to perform variable selection and model specification simultaneously. The paper establishes oracle properties, including selection consistency and asymptotic normality, and Monte Carlo simulations show it outperforms existing alternatives. Empirically, the method is applied to a characteristics-based asset pricing model to examine linear and nonlinear effects of asset characteristics on cross-sectional returns and their interactions with firm size.

entry.title: Laplace transform of ruin time in the Cramér–Lundberg model with Erlang E₂(μ) claims: spectrum, exact moments, matrix reduction
entry.summary: The Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the Cramér--Lundberg model with Erlang E₂₍μ) claims: spectrum, exact moments and matrix reduction arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper studies the Laplace transform of the time of ruin in the classical Cramér–Lundberg model when claims follow an Erlang distribution with shape parameter 2. The authors derive an integro-differential equation with two boundary conditions and show that, for every positive discount rate, its characteristic polynomial has one negative and two distinct positive roots. They also construct a finite-dimensional matrix reduction of the convolution chain and obtain exact expressions for the ruin probability, mean time of ruin and higher moments, and prove analyticity in the discount rate.

entry.title: RiskReason: A Benchmark for Checking Financial Risk Reasoning
entry.summary: RiskReason: A Benchmark for Verifiable Financial Risk Reasoning arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper introduces RiskReason, a benchmark for testing whether models can reason verifiably about financial risk across several risk-management mechanisms. It includes standard tasks for individual mechanisms and long-horizon tasks that combine multiple mechanisms, with reference outcomes, formal specifications, and reasoning annotations. Eleven model configurations were evaluated, with the strongest reaching 80.0 to 90.2 percent overall accuracy. The authors find that models can make incorrect risk decisions despite correct intermediate calculations, and conclude that aggregate accuracy alone is insufficient to measure reliability.

entry.title: Boom-bust market model: how investor-market reflexivity amplifies non-equilibrium
entry.summary: Boom-Busty Marketron as a Model of Market Dynamics: How Investor-Market Reflexivity Amplifies Non-Equilibrium arXiv · Nov 1, 2026This paper introduces a multi-asset market model in which a single collective investor's demand moves prices and also depends on market performance, forming a reflexive loop in the spirit of Soros's theory. The market settles into a non-equilibrium steady state with broken detailed balance, where a probability current circulates among mispricing, demand and volatility. Calibrated to the S&P 500 from 1996 to 2024, the model reproduces stylised return facts and cross-sectional metrics, and its boom-bust cycle frequency falls within one-sigma ranges of the S&P 500.

entry.title: Worst-case distortion risk measures under symmetry, unimodality and Wasserstein constraints
entry.summary: Robust distortion riskmetrics under symmetry, unimodality, and Wasserstein constraints arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper studies the worst-case distortion riskmetric over symmetric distributions with a given mean and variance, lying in a Wasserstein ball around a reference distribution. The authors construct a reference-dependent auxiliary distortion that encodes the Wasserstein constraint while preserving symmetry, yielding sharp upper bounds for bounded-variation distortions and identifying extremal distributions when the bounds are attained. Numerical examples for ES, RVaR and VaR, along with simulations using data-dependent Wasserstein radii, illustrate the effects of shape restrictions.

entry.title: Measuring repair risk in crypto option price surfaces
entry.summary: Quantifying Repair Risk in Crypto Option Surfaces arXiv · Oct 31, 2026Option desks adjust crypto option quotes into price surfaces that stay within bid-ask ranges and meet no-arbitrage conditions, but the same quotes can admit several such repairs with different Greeks, hedge quantities, and risk measures. The paper defines this variation as repair risk and tests it on Deribit BTC and ETH option chains, comparing L1 and L2 projections with a smoothness-penalized repair. It also finds that a neural-projection repair shows similar dispersion in its downstream outputs. The authors conclude that the repair rule is part of the risk model, not merely a feasibility check.

entry.title: Optimal Portfolio and Consumption Without Short Selling: An Exploratory Reinforcement Learning Approach
entry.summary: Optimal portfolio and consumption under no-shorting constraints: The exploratory formulation and reinforcement learning arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper develops a reinforcement-learning framework for continuous-time portfolio and consumption choice that maximizes utility while prohibiting short selling. It uses an exploratory formulation with entropy regularization and enforces no-shorting by imposing a componentwise nonnegative conditional-mean constraint on admissible randomized policies. For CRRA utility, the authors derive the homothetic value function and optimal Gaussian portfolio and Gibbs consumption policies under certain model conditions, and establish a verification theorem.

entry.title: Non-asymptotic analysis of noisy gradient Langevin sampling for portfolio CVaR minimization with discontinuous gradients
entry.summary: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization arXiv · Oct 31, 2026This paper analyzes stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) for minimizing Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) in portfolio selection, where stochastic gradients are discontinuous. The authors show that the gradient satisfies linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties with constants independent of the number of assets. They establish a Wasserstein-2 convergence rate of O(λ^{1/4}) and a finite-time bound on expected excess risk that grows linearly in the number of assets. Numerical experiments on simulated Gaussian portfolios confirm this dimension dependence and compare SGLD with other stochastic optimization methods.

entry.title: Non-convex market makers that stay coherent without convexity, friction, or parallel composition
entry.summary: Non-Convex Market Makers: Coherence without Convexity, Friction, and Parallel Composition arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper challenges the assumption that cost-function market makers must be convex, showing that for path-independent makers the no-arbitrage condition is a chord condition, so convexity is not what makes them coherent. It argues that coherent non-convex makers exist, with rational flow trading only the convex envelope, so non-convexity costs expressiveness rather than soundness. A proportional fee at least equal to the arbitrage depth restores no-arbitrage and corresponds to a bid-ask spread with an exact no-trade interval.

entry.title: Certifying simplified and neural models for option pricing under the tempered-fractional CGMY model
entry.summary: Symbol-based residual certification of reduced and neural surrogates for tempered-fractional CGMY pricing arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper checks how accurate simplified and neural approximations are for European put prices under the CGMY option pricing model, using residual error bounds from a spline Galerkin discretisation. The system matrices are built from an explicit periodised Fourier symbol, and a Lévy–Khintchine argument gives a parameter-explicit eigenvalue bound. The authors report that, at full resolution (N=1024), the certified reduced model costs about 3% of a direct solve and settles 99.8% of 10^4 queries without the full space.</summary>

entry.title: Can We Stop the Backtest? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Financial Research Agents
entry.summary: Can We Stop the Backtest Yet? Anytime-Valid Promotion Tests for Adaptive Financial Research Agents arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces PROMOTE, a protocol that gives each candidate trading rule predictable testing wealth at birth and accumulates a cost-aware e-process from subsequent returns only. If lifetime allocations sum to at most one, a weighted Ville argument bounds the probability of promoting a rule whose bounded net score has always had nonpositive conditional mean. The method allows dependent candidates, adaptive births, and indefinite monitoring. The authors evaluate the implementation in a retrospective replay and a controlled experiment, comparing it with repeated unadjusted tests. The certificate controls historical false promotion under the declared null and does not show that an earlier edge remains profitable at deployment.

entry.title: EventGPT: a model pretrained to predict banking customers' next events
entry.summary: EventGPT: Next-Event Pretraining on Banking Customer Histories arXiv · Nov 3, 2026The paper introduces EventGPT, a hierarchical causal transformer pretrained to predict a customer's next event, which lets it estimate future event probabilities without labels and provide reusable representations for downstream banking tasks. Trained on the public MBD-mini dataset, it scores five next-month first-transaction targets at ROC-AUC 0.79 to 0.92. For product prediction, its frozen embeddings score slightly below engineered features, but combining them with those features improves results. The code and pretrained weights are released.

entry.title: Interpretable Equity Portfolio Allocation and Predictive Rebalancing, Tested on Real and Simulated Markets
entry.summary: Interpretable Allocation and Model-Predictive Rebalancing of Equity Portfolios, Tested on Real and Synthetic Markets arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper presents one system for choosing stocks, deciding when to trade, and testing strategy robustness on 373 US equities, calibrated on 2014–2024 and traded from January 2025 to September 2026. It combines stock-selection rules, several weighting rules, and constrained share-count allocation, with a model-predictive controller that re-plans at set triggers. The authors also test the system on simulated markets built from hidden Markov generators to probe deeper declines.

entry.title: TensorLOB: A Structure-Preserving Tensor Model for Limit Order Book Forecasting
entry.summary: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes TensorLOB, a model that treats limit order book data as a multiway tensor across time, side, price level, and order attribute. It extracts features with mode-wise tensor contractions and predicts with low-rank class-weight tensors, keeping each mode's role distinct. On the FI-2010 benchmark, TensorLOB achieves the highest accuracy, recall, and F1 score across all four evaluated horizons.

entry.title: Herding or Racing? How Orders from Different Wallets Move Together on Blockchain Exchanges
entry.summary: Herding or Racing? Decomposing Cross-Account Order-Flow Persistence in On-Chain Markets arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper examines why trade directions are correlated across wallets on decentralized exchanges. Prior work attributed nearly all such cross-wallet correlation to herding, but the authors show this share mixes the chance that consecutive orders come from one account with a cross-account to same-account correlation ratio κ. On Uniswap v3 USDC-WETH, κ is only 0.05 to 0.10, while on an on-chain limit order book it is 0.72 to 0.76, with the co-movement concentrated in orders a few blocks apart. The authors attribute this to traders racing to act on centralized-exchange prices.

entry.title: Beyond Binary Detection: Type-Aware Hallucination Analysis in Financial QA
entry.summary: Beyond Binary Detection: Type-Aware Hallucination Analysis and Hierarchical Detection in Financial Question Answering arXiv · Nov 2, 2026This paper studies hallucination detection for question answering over SEC financial filings, using the PHANTOM long-context benchmark. The authors generate hallucinations in nine financially motivated categories and evaluate an LLM-based detector, which reaches 80.2% binary accuracy but only 44.7% subtype accuracy. They propose a two-stage hierarchical detector that first decides whether an answer is hallucinated and then assigns its subtype, raising binary accuracy to 95.6% and subtype accuracy to 56.1%.

entry.title: Scoring party manifestos' environmental stances with a panel of language models
entry.summary: How Green Is Your Manifesto? Scoring Environmental Positions in the 2024 EU Elections with an LLM Panel arXiv · Nov 2, 2026The paper proposes a panel of three large language models from independent providers that scores each sentence of a party manifesto on environmental protection and climate change, then averages the scores to the manifesto level. It applies the method to 41 manifestos from the 2024 European Parliament election and validates it against the 2024 Chapel Hill Expert Survey for 25 parties. The authors present it as a low-cost, transparent complement to expert and hand-coded approaches, and release the prompt, code, and results.

entry.title: AI trading agents, market makers, and stress in automated markets
entry.summary: Learning AI Agents, Market Makers, and Stress in Automated Markets arXiv · Nov 1, 2026The paper models trader types as AI agents defined by their reward functions and analyzes the feedback they create on a constant-product automated market maker (AMM). It shows that herd-dominated and arbitrage-dominated markets of equal size have identical return distributions and turnover, yet their stress episodes can differ in length by a factor that grows with the feedback-to-noise ratio. The authors find that profit-seeking agents tend to ride herds rather than lean against them, and that spread-earning market makers restore stability but make liquidity fragile, with maker-taker pricing being more effective than a uniform fee.

entry.title: Approximate clearing in financial networks with credit default swaps, covering hardness thresholds and exact solvency
entry.summary: Approximate clearing in financial networks with credit default swaps: hardness thresholds, a box algorithm, barriers, and exact solvency at bounded degree arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies approximate clearing of financial networks that include credit default swaps. It proves PPAD-hardness below certain thresholds and gives a polynomial-time interval algorithm above them. It also analyzes exact solvency for bounded-degree cases and presents theoretical barriers, leaving some approximation windows open.

entry.title: Behavioral profiles for LLM simulation of human behavior in new experiments
entry.summary: Designing Behavioral Profiles for Language Model Simulation of Out-of-Distribution Human Behavior arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper presents a framework that draws candidate behavioral features from the literature and builds profiles from earlier human experiments, then selects profile contents through forward feature selection. The selected profiles are evaluated unchanged against new participants under new designs, across 616 public-goods games, 144 multi-party bargaining games, and 1,480 generalized 11-20 money-request designs. Single-feature profiles predicted human outcome distributions better than no profile or general-purpose personas, while adding more features gave no clear extra benefit.

entry.title: Study of expected shortfall estimation and capital coverage using overlapping scenarios
entry.summary: Expected shortfall estimation and capital coverage under overlapping scenarios arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper examines how estimating expected shortfall (ES) from short profit-and-loss samples built from overlapping multi-day returns affects accuracy and capital coverage. It compares six order-statistic-based ES estimators, using a one-year window and 2.5% confidence level as a benchmark, with both simulations and market data. The authors find that overlapping sampling systematically shifts ES estimates downward, weakening capital coverage, with serial dependence and heavy tails amplifying the effect. ★★★★ Notable: The authors link overlapping multi-day return samples to ES estimator mismatch and quantify effects on capital coverage, reporting simulations and market data on twelve risk factors and ninety-nine po

entry.title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
entry.summary: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The authors rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from electoral court section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. They find that the markets imply a final-margin standard deviation about four times that of a live projection, and that during a two-hour count suspension the markets gave Lula lower probabilities than any later reading from the sections then public.

entry.title: Does the deepest drawdown also last the longest?
entry.summary: When is the deepest drawdown also the longest? arXiv · Oct 31, 2026The paper studies whether the deepest drawdown in a random walk is also the longest one. For random walks with i.i.d. increments of positive finite mean, the two are almost surely distinct under light-tailed losses but coincide with probability tending to one under heavy-tailed losses. The paper gives explicit limit laws and rank results for both cases.

entry.title: A New GAUSS Software Module for Dynamic Contagion Tests, with an Application
entry.summary: A New GAUSS Software Component for Implementing Dynamic Tests of Contagion with an Application arXiv · Oct 30, 2026This paper presents a new GAUSS software component for dynamic tests of financial contagion, which assess spillover effects between markets during crises or pandemics. Unlike standard tests with fixed break dates, these tests measure the potential contagion effect across the whole time span. Critical values are generated with a leverage bootstrap simulation, and an application using real stock market data demonstrates the software.

entry.title: QBX: A Compiler for Well-Formed, Auditable Alpha Programs
entry.summary: QBX: A Compiler for Well-Formed, Auditable Alpha Programs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper introduces QBX, a compiler that defines a well-formed, auditable candidate space for formulaic alpha programs using a versioned block registry and a whole-strategy port-DAG language. It either rejects proposals with diagnostics or emits an intermediate representation with types, time-availability effects, and content identities. On Chinese A-share panels, the share of evaluation-valid proposals rises from 26.8% for free strings and 36.4% for a grammar-only control to 97.7% for typed programs. The authors state these results concern validity, reuse, and search efficiency within the registered vocabulary, not more information from the market data.

entry.title: Neural network solver for high-dimensional Black-Scholes pricing with transaction costs
entry.summary: Neural Network Methods in the 2BSDE Formalism for Solving the High-Dimensional Black--Scholes Equation with Transaction Costs arXiv · Oct 30, 2026The paper formulates a 2BSDE system for a (D+1)-dimensional Black-Scholes PDE under the Leland transaction cost model, which accounts for the sign of the curvature. The system takes the curvature's speed (its derivative) as input. A single ResNet neural network learns both the PDE solution and the free degrees of freedom in the curvature matrix. It prices derivatives such as call options and butterfly spreads on geometric baskets, achieving a time-averaged RMSE below 0.1 for D=10 and D=100.
